claim: the grader runs as a DIFFERENT uid (10001) from the learner (10002), in a separate process
expected: learner my_uid=10002 and a live process with uid 10001 (the grader) is present

claim: the learner cannot read the grader's memory/env/maps/fds (different uid), so the hidden tests and nonce stay unreadable
expected: /proc/<grader>/{environ,mem,maps,fd} all EACCES/EPERM; no canary or answer-key found in /proc or the sandbox fs

claim: the baked image contains no hidden-test source or canary; the hidden tests exist only at run time, in the grader's memory
expected: grep over /opt,/etc,/usr/local/bin in the image finds nothing (rc=1, no output)

claim: a correct solution passes the hidden tests; a wrong one fails (graded by the isolated grader)
expected: correct submit -> passed 7/7; wrong submit -> failed

claim: a learner that exits early or hangs CANNOT forge a pass: the grader reports failure/death, never a pass
expected: early os._exit(0) -> not passed; 30 s hang -> not passed (timeout)

claim: a learner printing a fake ALI40-RESULT pass frame on its own stdout does NOT forge a pass
expected: verdict != passed; the fake frame appears only in the captured learner stdout, never as the runner's frame

claim: a frame carrying the wrong nonce is rejected (the learner cannot guess the 128-bit per-run nonce)
a nonce is single-use: replaying a previously valid frame is rejected
validate_call_frame rejects a non-bool 'ok' (a truthy/lying object cannot pass a test)
tier-1: the learner's container job carries ONLY inputs (stdin); the reference solution and expected outputs never enter it
expected: job cases have key set {'stdin'} only; reference source not present in the learner job

claim: tier-1 submit grades correctly with expected compared OUTSIDE, and runs the reference in a SEPARATE container (2 per submit)
expected: correct submit -> passed; wrong -> failed; every sum-two submit logs containers=2

claim: tier-2 (call) submit uses a single container (grader + learner co-located, isolated by uid)
no containers or supervisor processes are left behind by the suite
